title: FIRST AID
overview: This practical course introduces essential first aid knowledge and skills for responding to common medical emergencies and workplace injuries until qualified emergency services take over. Participants learn to recognize hazards, protect themselves and the casualty, activate the local emergency response system, assess responsiveness and breathing, and provide appropriate initial assistance within their training and organizational procedures. The program emphasizes realistic scenarios, supervised skills practice, clear communication and timely handover. It is an introductory training course; any formal first aid or CPR/AED certification depends on the applicable accrediting body and separate assessment requirements.
audience: Security personnel, facilities and operations staff, office employees, reception and customer-facing teams, supervisors, health and safety representatives, designated workplace first aiders, and employees who may be required to provide initial assistance during an emergency.
methodology: Instructor-led demonstrations, guided practice with appropriate training equipment, emergency-response scenarios, casualty-assessment drills, simulated emergency calls, paired skills exercises, group discussions, case studies, and formative practical feedback. CPR and AED skills are practiced using suitable training manikins and devices where available, following the current protocols adopted by the training provider.
competencies: Early recognition of medical emergencies and prompt activation of emergency services
Basic CPR and AED awareness and practice
Management of choking and severe bleeding
Initial care for common injuries and sudden illness
Effective incident communication, documentation and handover
objectives: Identify hazards, apply basic infection-prevention measures and establish a safe response area.
Explain the first aider’s role, limitations, consent considerations and when to call emergency services.
Perform a structured initial assessment of responsiveness and normal breathing.
Demonstrate CPR and AED use on training equipment in accordance with the course protocol.
Recognize choking and apply age-appropriate response principles within the scope of training.
Apply initial measures for severe external bleeding and suspected shock.
Describe appropriate responses to burns, fractures, head injuries and other common incidents.
Recognize warning signs of time-critical illnesses and seek urgent professional assistance.
Monitor and reassure a casualty while preparing an accurate emergency handover.
